clue.text: What one thinks can be found on picture-postcard

definitions.meaning: an opinion or way of seeing a matter
the scenic vista pictured on the front of a holiday card

explanation.surface: Musing on where your opinions can be read: perhaps on a holiday card.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is one's outlook, and a picture-postcard typically shows a scenic outlook.

indicators.note: the clue says saving is the word in plus this, so taking that word away leaves what this stands for

parts.note: money put by as savings is an investment
the little word in, taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrifty person saves money by sticking to one item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Saving (INVESTMENT) is IN plus this': remove IN from the front and what is left is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a robe or item of clothing, especially one worn by clergy.

parts.note: timber is wood
a cock is a small conical pile of hay, a haycock

explanation.surface: A bird emerges from a heap of logs.
explanation.walkthrough: A cock (as in haycock) is a cone-shaped heap of hay in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a long-billed wading bird of woodland.

clue.text: One who does light work arranging marriages

definitions.meaning: a maker of the sticks struck to light fires
one who brings couples together for weddings

explanation.surface: Someone with an easy job fixing up weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' looks like 'easy work', but it means making things that give light: matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory hand producing matches and a go-between who pairs couples share the same title.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Maria is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of DOLT and MARIA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit is a synonym of awkward or inept.

parts.note: a transistor is a semiconductor device
a set is a radio or television receiver

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a kit of electronic components.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a radio set built around semiconductors.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable wireless receiver using transistors, which are semiconductor devices.

definitions.meaning: a coming together of people, a get-together
fulfilling, as in fulfilling a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: Describing a rendezvous that turns out to be rewarding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering is an encounter, and one fulfilling a need is said to be doing so in the sense of meeting it.

clue.text: Bit yokel removed, part of computer's memory

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are moved around from their places, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin has been taken out by a computer component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved: the letters of BIT YOKEL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilobyte is a unit of computer storage of about a thousand bytes.

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the county name

explanation.surface: Something protrudes in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridgeshire is a famously flat English county, which makes the surface amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised strip of land that rises above its surroundings.

definitions.meaning: a place where pupils are educated
a group of fish swimming together

explanation.surface: A place of learning with a swimming squad.
explanation.definitionFit: The educational establishment and a shoal of fish share the same word.

parts.note: in cricket, the fielders ask the umpire whether a batsman is out

explanation.surface: Was someone invited on a date?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asked out' suggests a date; in cricket the fielding side shouts to the umpire to have a batsman given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielders who call 'Howzat?' to the umpire are making a request for a dismissal.

clue.text: Care about this in Paris that had been cut into small pieces

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for care goes round the French word

parts.note: to care is to mind
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Someone takes care of a Parisian dish that had been chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CE inside MIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat is chopped very finely.

clue.text: One does not expect to see this from a good writer

definitions.text: One does not expect to see this from a good writer

parts.words: One does not expect to see this from a good writer
parts.note: a writer with good handwriting does not produce untidy marks

explanation.surface: Something a fine author would never turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good writer' suggests an accomplished author, but it means someone with neat handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty, illegible handwriting is what neat penmanship avoids.

clue.text: Pelican perhaps going over the water

definitions.meaning: a pelican is a UK pedestrian road ... with lights
a journey across a sea or river

explanation.surface: A bird flies over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing controlled by push-button traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican is one kind of pedestrian street crossing, and a sea passage is also called by the same name.

parts.note: a small scrubbing tool used on the ends of the fingers

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that is always handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one's fingertips' means readily available, but literally it is where this cleaner works.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stiff brush for scrubbing under fingernails works at the tips of the fingers.

parts.note: tea is the leaves of the tea plant
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Lord Kelvin departs, leaving some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard timber from a tropical tree.

definitions.meaning: someone or something that sets or corrects a mechanism
an insurance assessor is often a loss assessor, the phrase loss coming first

explanation.surface: A controller who frequently doesn't know what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a loss' suggests puzzlement; the word frequently follows 'loss' in the job of an insurance assessor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sets things right regulates them, and insurance claims are assessed by a loss assessor of the same title.

clue.text: Short passage from the bible, the words are appearing on the computer screen

definitions.meaning: a verse chosen as the subject of a sermon

definitions.text: the words are appearing on the computer screen
definitions.meaning: the written content shown on a display

explanation.surface: A Bible verse displayed on a monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher's chosen verse and the written content on a screen share the same word.

definitions.meaning: an indication that gives something away
someone who blabs secrets, a sneak

explanation.surface: An indication of an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A revealing indication and a sneak who gossips share the same word.

definitions.meaning: prepared to put up with something
play in engineering is permitted slack, which a part with tolerance allows

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drama is something one can sit through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like drama, but in engineering it is permitted slack, so something allowing play is lenient in that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient and forbearing people put up with things, and a fitting allowing play is forgiving of movement.

clue.text: Poison appears when a protein disintegrates

indicators.note: disintegrates means falls to pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A toxin is formed when a protein breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disintegrates' rearranges A PROTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: Taking a pace over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side of something is being across it.

definitions.meaning: shorter and stouter
a person crouching on their haunches

explanation.surface: A rather stout person taking a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and thick means squat, so more so is the comparative; someone crouching is also a squatter.

indicators.note: removed suggests letters moved about again, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An impassive Scot gets taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, rearranging SCOT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures pain without showing feelings.

clue.text: Worker took Elizabeth into the country

indicators.note: took means held within, so the word for worker contains the name

parts.note: a bee is a worker, as in a worker bee
Liz is short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An employee brought Elizabeth into the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Belize is a country in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a Central American nation on the Caribbean.

clue.text: Lea striking first near the boundary

indicators.note: first means the word for striking goes before the word for lea

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a lea is a meadow, a field

explanation.surface: A meadow on strike at the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the outfield is the part of the ground near the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the part of the ground furthest from the wicket lies close to the boundary rope.

clue.text: High-class horse backed by attorney in Africa

parts.note: U means upper-class

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the word for horse is reversed

parts.note: a nag is a horse
DA is district attorney

explanation.surface: A posh horse supported by a lawyer in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns NAG into GAN. 'backed' suggests a horse bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a country in East Africa.

clue.text: One of the larvae found in a pile?

definitions.text: One of the larvae found in a pile?

parts.words: One of the larvae found in a pile?
parts.note: the pile is the soft surface of a floor covering where certain grubs feed

explanation.surface: A grub found in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' suggests a heap, but it is the nap of a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect's larvae feed on the woollen nap of floor coverings.

definitions.meaning: in earlier times, once
used before a name to mean previously, as an archaic prefix

explanation.surface: A word repeated for emphasis on old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word for once or previously, also used in erstwhile.
